1367.title: KS-1015: the referral lookup spec declares the envelope its handler returns
1367.head: ac3ceee7f440478431a317d3a31a42ab737f57c7
commits:
KS-1015: the referral lookup spec declares the envelope its handler returns

GET /api/referrals/{code} published the flat ReferralCode record as its 200 body,
while the handler in routes/referrals.ts answers a success/data envelope with a
public projection: code, isActive, isExpired, referredReward and referrerReward
always, customLabel only when set. Schemathesis flagged the 200 as
response_schema_conformance. The spec now follows the runtime.

id and ownerUserId are left out on purpose: this is a public lookup. The
ReferralCode component stays published and the owner list
(GET /api/referrals/user/{userId}) still returns it.

One new vitest file renders the document the generator publishes from the shared
registry and asserts the envelope, its six fields and their runtime types, with
three controls covering bearerAuth, the ReferralCode component and the sibling
POST /generate 201 envelope. docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml is regenerated by
npm run generate-openapi; check:openapi is clean.
1367.body:
Refs KS-1015

One carve out of the KS-1015 sweep, not the whole of it. KS-1015 covers 28 unowned
check/operation pairs; this is ONE of them, `GET /api/referrals/{code}`. It narrows the
ticket and does not close it.

## What was wrong
The published contract declared the flat `ReferralCode` record (id, code, ownerUserId,
uses, ...) as the 200 body. The handler (`services/referral/src/routes/referrals.ts`,
`GET /:code`) answers `{ success, data: { code, isActive, isExpired, customLabel,
referredReward, referrerReward } }`. Schemathesis flagged the 200 as
`response_schema_conformance`.

`id` and `ownerUserId` are left out of the response on purpose — this is a public lookup —
so the spec follows the runtime rather than the other way round. `ReferralCodeSchema` stays
exactly where it was for the owner list (`GET /api/referrals/user/{userId}`), which still
returns the flat record.

## What changed — 3 files
- `services/referral/src/referral.openapi.ts` (+21/-1): the 200 content becomes the
  success/data envelope with the six fields the handler sends, `customLabel` optional,
  `.passthrough()` on the data object.
- `services/referral/src/__tests__/ks1015-referral-lookup-spec-declares-envelope.test.ts`
  (+76, new): renders the document the generator publishes from the shared registry and
  asserts the envelope. No server, no database, no network.
- `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` (+30/-1): regenerated by `npm run generate-openapi`.
  Not hand-edited.

## Test Evidence

**Touched:** `services/referral/src/referral.openapi.ts`, one new test under
`services/referral/src/__tests__/`, `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`.

**Ran** (all local, on this branch's head, after `npm ci --ignore-scripts` at the
`Blockchain/Dev` workspace root plus `npm run build` in `packages/shared`):
- `vitest run` in `services/referral` BEFORE the change, on a pristine tree at the base
  commit: **6 files / 28 tests / 28 passed**, rc 0.
- `vitest run` in `services/referral` AFTER: **7 files / 34 tests / 34 passed**, rc 0.
- Red-first, by assertion: with the product hunk reverted and the test kept,
  **3 failed | 3 passed (6)** — the three RED cells fail with real assertion errors and the
  three controls pass. The total stays 6, so the file loads; a 0-passed-and-0-failed result
  would have been a load failure, not a red.
- `npm run generate-openapi` rc 0; the regenerated YAML is byte-identical to an independent
  `patch(1)` reconstruction of the same change onto the base YAML
  (39,889 lines, sha256 `43c71cf6d5f213b6`).
- `npm run check:openapi` rc 0 — `CHECK PASS: on-disk YAML matches generated`, and
  `check-spec-examples` reports 405 example blocks, all resolving. Control: with the YAML
  reverted to base the same check goes rc 1 (`CHECK FAIL`), so the pass is a reading.
- `tsc --noEmit` for `services/referral`: rc 0 at the base commit and rc 0 at this head —
  reported as a no-regression comparison only.
- The pre-push preflight: `PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 12/15 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing
  failed.` All three skips are `SKIP — local stack not up on http://localhost:6882 (start
  it to run this leg)`. No `--no-verify`.

**NOT run / NOT covered:**
- No Schemathesis run and no live run against a running stack. The claim here is about the
  document the generator publishes, not about a response observed on the wire.
- The served `/api/docs/openapi.json` was not read. Only the generated
  `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` was compared.
- `tsc` does **not** type-check the new test: the service tsconfig's `exclude` is
  `["node_modules", "dist", "src/__tests__"]`. So the rc 0 above covers service source only.
- The three skipped preflight legs above were not run.
- The other 27 pairs in the KS-1015 sweep are untouched by this PR.
- The KS 255 Schemathesis baseline is not re-baselined here; that estate is not this PR's.

**Migrations + config:** none. No migration, no schema change, no environment variable, no
lockfile change, no dependency change, no `scripts/audit` baseline change.

## Sequencing
A sibling PR for the KS 1364 residue is raised from the same base commit. Both touch
`docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, at hunks more than 3,000 lines apart, so their YAML edits
never share context. This one lands first.

1368.title: KS-1364: mark two more request bodies required where handlers reject an absent body
1368.head: 2a3dcd912a33b1ced6b6769368d87fce82ab64bc
commits:
KS-1364: mark two more request bodies required where handlers reject an absent body

Two of the remaining six operations from the sweep. Both handlers reject an absent or
empty body with a 400, so the published contract now says the body is required.

PATCH /api/platform/tenants/{id} — the handler builds its SET list from the fields
present and answers 400 with BAD_REQUEST "No fields to update" when none are
(tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:455-457), so an empty object is already refused.

POST /api/v2/verification/verify — the handler needs at least one of documentId, a
content hash or documentData and answers 400 BAD_REQUEST otherwise
(originate/src/routes/verificationV2.ts:452-456). It accepts four spellings of the
hash — hash, providedHash, contentHash and documentHash (:450-:451) — and every one
of them is optional individually, which is why the schema stays as it is and only the
body-level required flag changes.

One new test per operation renders the document the generator publishes from the shared
registry and asserts the required flag, each with three controls covering the schema,
the route's security and a sibling operation. docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml is
regenerated by npm run generate-openapi, taking the two required flags to 73.

This leaves four of the seventeen operations. POST /api/referrals/generate is
deliberately not among them: its generateCodeSchema has four optional fields and the
route calls .parse(req.body) directly (referral/src/routes/referrals.ts:16-21, :61), so
an empty object satisfies it and a body genuinely is not required there. The other three
are auth surfaces excluded by scope.
1368.body:
Refs KS-1364

Two of the remaining six operations from the sweep. **This does not close the ticket**:
13 of its 17 operations are covered once this lands, and four are left.

## The two operations, and why each is safe to mark
Both handlers already refuse an absent or empty body with a 400, so declaring the body
required makes the contract agree with the runtime rather than changing behaviour.

**PATCH /api/platform/tenants/{id}** — the handler builds its SET list from whichever
fields are present and answers `400 BAD_REQUEST "No fields to update"` when none are
(`services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:455-457`). An empty object is already refused.

**POST /api/v2/verification/verify** — the handler requires at least one of `documentId`,
a content hash, or `documentData`, and answers `400 BAD_REQUEST` otherwise
(`services/originate/src/routes/verificationV2.ts:452-456`). It accepts **four** spellings
of the hash — `hash`, `providedHash`, `contentHash` and `documentHash` — coalesced at
`:450-451`. Each is individually optional, which is exactly why the request *schema* is
unchanged here and only the body-level `required` flag moves.

## What is NOT in this PR, and why — POST /api/referrals/generate
It is deliberately left unmarked. `generateCodeSchema` has four `.optional()` fields
(`services/referral/src/routes/referrals.ts:16-21`) and the route calls
`generateCodeSchema.parse(req.body)` directly (`:61`), so `{}` satisfies the schema and a
body genuinely is not required. Marking it would make the spec disagree with the handler.
An absent-body probe answered 201 for this route, against a replica of the gate rather
than the running app.

The other three left are auth surfaces, excluded by scope: `POST /api/issuer-certs`,
`PATCH /api/users/admin/{id}` and `POST /api/users/me/change-password`.

## What changed — 5 files
- `services/tenant-provisioning/src/tenant-provisioning.openapi.ts` (+1/-0): one
  `required: true` on the PATCH request body.
- `services/originate/src/originate.openapi.ts` (+1/-0): the same on the v2 verify body.
- Two new tests (+48 and +46), one per operation, each rendering the generated document
  and asserting the flag, with three controls apiece.
- `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` (+2/-0): regenerated, taking the count of
  `required: true` body flags from 71 to 73. Not hand-edited.

## Test Evidence

**Touched:** the two `*.openapi.ts` files above, two new tests under each service's
`src/__tests__/`, and `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`.

**Ran** (all local, on this branch's head, after `npm ci --ignore-scripts` at the
`Blockchain/Dev` workspace root plus `npm run build` in `packages/shared`):
- `vitest run` in `services/tenant-provisioning`: BEFORE on a pristine tree at the base
  commit **3 files / 13 tests / 13 passed**; AFTER **4 files / 17 tests / 17 passed**. rc 0 both.
- `jest` in `services/originate`: BEFORE **89 suites / 1058 tests / 1058 passed**; AFTER
  **90 suites / 1062 tests / 1062 passed**. rc 0 both.
- Red-first, by assertion, per operation with only that product hunk reverted:
  tenant-provisioning **1 failed | 3 passed (4)**, originate **1 failed, 3 passed, 4 total**.
  Each red is a real assertion failure and each total stays at 4, so both files load — a
  0-passed-and-0-failed result would have been a load failure rather than a red. Green
  after: 4/4 and 4/4.
- `npm run generate-openapi` rc 0. The regenerated YAML is byte-identical to an independent
  `patch(1)` reconstruction of the same two changes onto the base YAML
  (39,862 lines, sha256 `39f027b63d4aa804`).
- `npm run check:openapi` rc 0 — `CHECK PASS`, and `check-spec-examples` reports 405 example
  blocks all resolving. Control: with the YAML reverted to base the same check goes rc 1
  (`CHECK FAIL`), so the pass is a reading. `--check` wrote nothing.
- `tsc --noEmit` rc 0 for both services, reported as a no-regression reading only.
- Both applied diffs were compared byte-for-byte against an independent `patch(1)` apply of
  the same changes, and each strict `git apply --check` was paired with a tamper that was
  measured to make it fail.
- The pre-push preflight ran in-hook with no `--no-verify`.

**NOT run / NOT covered:**
- No Schemathesis run and no live run against a running stack. The claim is about the
  document the generator publishes, not a response observed on the wire.
- The absent-body behaviour cited above was measured against a **replica** of each gate at
  `body-parser` 1.20.6. The version these services actually lock is **1.20.8** (root,
  originate and tenant-provisioning locks all resolve `body-parser` 1.20.8), so the probe
  and the shipped parser are not the same build.
- The served `/api/docs/openapi.json` was not read; only the generated YAML was compared.
- `tsc` type-checks **neither** new test: tenant-provisioning excludes `src/__tests__`, and
  originate excludes `src/__tests__`, `src/**/*.test.ts` and `src/**/*.integration.test.ts`.
- The four remaining operations are untouched.
- The KS 255 Schemathesis baseline is not re-baselined here, and that estate is not this
  PR's to change.

**Migrations + config:** none. No migration, no schema change, no environment variable, no
lockfile change, no dependency change, no audit-baseline change.

## Sequencing
Lands after PR A (#1367). Both PRs are cut from the same base commit as siblings — this one
is not built on A's branch and is not rebased onto A's merge. Both touch
`docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, but their hunks sit at roughly YAML lines 28,969 / 32,174 /
35,544, so the nearest pair is 3,205 lines apart and their edits never share context.

The tree this PR lands as after A is **`48f5f8afa6ef1f03f2d64e4afa24fd9f75213ad7`**, proved
rather than assumed: `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the two heads reports no conflicts, and
independently assembling that tree (A's head plus this PR's full diff) produces a YAML whose
object id equals the merge-tree's YAML blob exactly, at 39,891 lines and 73 `required: true`
body flags, with `check:openapi` rc 0 on it.

Foreign keys in this description are deliberately written without a hyphen (KS 1015, KS 255,
KS 442) so they neither move nor attach.
